ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: Raid Redesigner — Old Friends
ModMetaData.author: Mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
PLOT_MECHANISM_MODS_WAVE_1 — the persistent-NPC roster half of design/Jawa/proposals/plot_mechanisms_wave.md §1.4, ruled in scope 2026-09-05. Ships ONLY `GameComponent_OldFriends`: a scribed roster of `OldFriendEntry` records (pawn, faction-at-entry, role tag, encounter list, grudge, notability, last-seen tick, dead flag), capped at 24 living entries (lowest notability pruned; dead entries collapse to one line and stay), and eight Harmony postfix hooks that each write one Encounter at a real vanilla or sibling-mod seam: a raider fleeing the map, a raid captain leaving, a prisoner escaping, a prisoner being released, a caravan/visitor robbed (mandrake.rm.property's TakingEvent), a colonist kidnapped, and a Blackstar (vanilla Pirate faction, reskinned) guest-status change tagged NAMED_HUNTER. The ninth row in the design doc's table — a woken ancient leaving — is STUBBED: no vanilla or sibling-mod signal fires reliably for it yet (RimUtinni: VaultDungeons' own About.xml says as much: "V6's wake/loot branches listen on signals no vanilla part sends yet"), so RoleTag.WokenAncient exists and the hook point is a documented no-op rather than an invented signal.
Pinning: a recalled/recorded pawn who leaves the map is pinned against world-pawn GC via `Find.WorldPawns.PassToWorld(pawn, PawnDiscardDecideMode.KeepForever)` — the same call vanilla's own `Faction` uses to keep a faction leader alive indefinitely (verified against 1.6 source before writing).
No LLM, no menu authority, no letter rewrite, no defs. Pure C# bookkeeping infrastructure that four other design arcs (Reclamation, Blackstar truce, the woken claim, recurring villains) read later. Part 1's redesign layer proper (Harmony seams A/B/C on the raid pipeline, the Oracle prompt contract) is explicitly OUT of this mod, held pending the owner's own Oracle-promotion decision.
